messages:
Elena: Heads-up: current month we have a $12.3k committed GPU pool underutilization (reserved capacity 'orion-reserved'). Team Orion used ~18% of the commitment, so the amortized committed cost is creating a $9.8k internal variance. Asking for ideas on reallocation.

cost-bot: ALERT: Reserved-pool utilization <25% for pool=orion-reserved (billing month-to-date). Potential waste: $9,800. See FIN-5078.

Sam: Quick summary: Orion reserved 8x A100s for 1yr (committed). Usage telemetry shows most GPUs idle; some VMs were retired without releasing the reservation. We can reassign capacity but cloud provider requires pool-owner change requests and accounting notes.

Rohit: Product would like to borrow capacity for Atlas model rollout (short spike next 3 weeks). Can we do a temporary transfer of reserved units to Atlas so we avoid on-demand spend?

Ivy: From Sales: if we reassign part of Orion commitment to Atlas and a customer-facing job runs under Atlas, do we need to notify the customer or change contract terms? We must ensure customer billing isn't affected.

Nadia: Legal: provider reservations are billed to Redwood; internal transfers are accounting-only. Check the provider TOS: if we move capacity across projects we must maintain audit trail. Also if any customer-specific commitments exist, we need to ensure no passthrough.

Sam: Two options: (A) internal amortization: keep reservation on Orion account and spread monthly committed cost across teams by a fixed formula (based on forecasted consumption); (B) change pool assignment with provider (requires provider support ticket and up to 7-day processing). Option B avoids on-demand delta, but has process overhead.

Elena: Finance preference is Option A for auditability unless a >30-day reassign is needed. For short term (<=21 days) we can do a manual internal reallocation: credit Orion and bill Atlas a portion of amortized committed cost. Approval required for reallocations > $5k.

Rohit: Atlas needs about 20% of the pool for the next 3 weeks (~1.6 GPUs equivalent). That maps to ~ $3.1k of committed cost amortization. Falls under $5k so can proceed with finance approval.

Ivy: Confirming: customer-facing workloads will run under Atlas project; we must ensure we don't inadvertently bill customer usage to internal commit credits. Add a flag on the job to mark "customer_pass_through" so reporting separates customer-billed hours.

Sam: I'll add a job tag `commit_alloc=atlas_temp` and an instance label `customer_pass_through=true|false`. Also will create a provider support ticket if we decide to do Pool Reassignment B.

Elena: Approval: I approve a one-time internal reallocation of $3.1k from Orion to Atlas for up to 21 days. Please create FIN ticket and attach the expected usage window and owner sign-off.

Nadia: Add legal note: keep provider communications and add statement in FIN ticket that no customer contracts are being amended. If provider requires signature, loop me in.

InfraScheduler: NOTE: Temporary allocation applied to tracking table: pool=orion-reserved, allocation=atlas_temp, start=2025-06-01, end=2025-06-22 (metadata only). This does not change provider reservation.

Sam: Action items: (1) I'll tag the Atlas jobs and patch deploy templating (today), (2) Elena will open FIN-5078 reallocation line item with $3.1k credit (done), (3) Nadia on standby if provider asks for legal sign-off.

Elena: Thanks. If actual Atlas consumption exceeds forecast and the reallocation would go >$5k, we'll pause and re-evaluate provider pool reassignment. Keep monitoring in FIN-5078.

Rohit: Will monitor and post daily usage highlights to this thread.

cost-bot: SCHEDULED: Reserved-utilization monitoring job will post daily at 04:30 UTC.

Elena: Closing note: good example of preferring accounting reallocation for short windows to avoid provider churn. Will document the playbook after this run. :white_check_mark:
